#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""commonmark: read UTF-8 Markdown on stdin and write HTML to stdout."""

import os
import sys

270	)
271	# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes
272	# as soon as the next line arrives.
273	THEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(
274	    "thematic_break",
275	    continues=_never_continues,
276	    start=_thematic_break_start,
277	)
278	# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as
279	# inlines when the document is rendered.
280	ATX_HEADING = BlockType(
281	    "atx_heading",
282	    continues=_never_continues,
283	    start=_atx_heading_start,
284	)
285	
286	
287	CODE_INDENT = 4
288	
289	
290	def _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
291	    """Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.
292	
293	    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and
294	    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.
295	    """
296	    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:
297	        return None
298	    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
299	    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)
300	
301	
302	def _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
303	    """A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.
304	
305	    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.
306	    """
307	    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
308	        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
309	        return True
310	    return False
311	
312	
313	def _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
314	    """Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns."""
315	    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)
316	
317	
318	def _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
319	    """Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content."""
320	    lines = list(block.lines)
321	    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):
322	        lines.pop()
323	    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)
324	
325	
326	# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
327	# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.
328	INDENTED_CODE = BlockType(
329	    "indented_code",
330	    continues=_indented_code_continues,
331	    accepts_lines=True,
332	    start=_indented_code_start,
333	    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,
334	    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,
335	)
336	
337	
338	FENCE_CHARS = "`~"
339	FENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3
340	BACKTICK = "`"
341	
342	
343	@dataclass
344	class Fence:
345	    """The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.
346	
347	    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from
348	    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True
349	    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing
350	    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.
351	    """
352	
353	    char: str
354	    length: int
355	    indent: int
356	    language: str
357	    opening: bool = True
358	    closed: bool = False
359	
360	
361	def _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:
362	    """Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`."""
363	    end = start
364	    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:
365	        end += 1
366	    return end
367	
368	
369	def _language(info: str) -> str:
370	    """The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or ""."""
371	    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()
372	    return words[0] if words else ""
373	
374	
375	def _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
376	    """Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.
377	
378	    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.
379	    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the
380	    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.
381	    """
382	    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
383	        return None
384	    line = cursor.line
385	    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
386	    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:
387	        return None
388	    char = line[start]
389	    end = _run_end(line, start, char)
390	    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:
391	        return None
392	    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)
393	    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:
394	        return None
395	    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))
396	    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
397	    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)
398	    block.fence = fence
399	    return block
400	
401	
402	def _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:
403	    """True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.
404	
405	    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three
406	    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.
407	    """
408	    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
409	        return False
410	    line = cursor.line
411	    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
412	    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)
413	    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)
414	
415	
416	def _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
417	    """Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.
418	
419	    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening
420	    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.
421	    """
422	    fence = block.fence
423	    assert fence is not None
424	    if fence.closed:
425	        return False
426	    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):
427	        fence.closed = True
428	        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))
429	        return True
430	    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)
431	    return True
432	
433	
434	def _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
435	    """Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing."""
436	    fence = block.fence
437	    assert fence is not None
438	    if fence.opening:
439	        fence.opening = False
440	        return
441	    if fence.closed:
442	        return
443	    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)
444	
445	
446	def _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
447	    """Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.
448	
449	    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.
450	    """
451	    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in block.lines)
452	
453	
454	# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
455	# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's
456	# container.
457	FENCED_CODE = BlockType(
458	    "fenced_code",
459	    continues=_fenced_code_continues,
460	    accepts_lines=True,
461	    start=_fenced_code_start,
462	    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,
463	    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,
464	)
465	
466	
467	class BlockRegistry:
468	    """The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.
469	
470	    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no
471	    start rule matches a line of text.
472	    """
473	
474	    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:
475	        self.root = root
476	        self.fallback = fallback
477	        self._names: set[str] = set()
478	        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []
479	        self.register(root)
480	        self.register(fallback)
481	
482	    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:
483	        """Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order."""
484	        if block_type.name in self._names:
485	            raise ValueError(f"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}")
486	        self._names.add(block_type.name)
487	        if block_type.start is not None:
488	            self._starts.append(block_type)
489	
490	    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:
491	        """The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order."""
492	        return tuple(self._starts)
493	
494	
495	DEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)
496	DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)
497	DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)
498	DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)
499	DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)
500	
501	
502	class DocumentParser:
503	    """Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time."""
504	
505	    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:
506	        self.registry = registry
507	        self.root = Block(registry.root)
508	        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()
509	
510	    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:
511	        """Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text."""
512	        cursor = Cursor(line)
513	
514	        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.
515	        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)
516	        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None
517	
518	        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.
519	        started = False
520	        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):
521	            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)
522	            if new_block is None:
523	                break
524	            if not started:
525	                started = True
526	                all_closed = True
527	                self._close_below(container)
528	            self._attach(new_block, container)
529	            container = new_block
530	
531	        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.
532	        tip = self._tip()
533	        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:
534	            self._add_line(tip, cursor)
535	            return
536	        self._close_below(container)
537	        if container.kind.accepts_lines:
538	            self._add_line(container, cursor)
539	        elif not cursor.is_blank():
540	            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)
541	            self._attach(paragraph, container)
542	            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)
543	
544	    def finish(self) -> Block:
545	        """Close every open block and return the document root."""
546	        self._close_below(self.root)
547	        self.root.is_open = False
548	        return self.root
549	
550	    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:
551	        container = self.root
552	        while True:
553	            child = container.open_last_child()
554	            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):
555	                return container
556	            container = child
557	
558	    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
559	        for block_type in self.registry.starts():
560	            assert block_type.start is not None
561	            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)
562	            if new_block is not None:
563	                return new_block
564	        return None
565	
566	    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:
567	        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible
568	
569	    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:
570	        """Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it."""
571	        while not container.kind.is_container:
572	            self._finalize(container)
573	            assert container.parent is not None
574	            container = container.parent
575	        container.children.append(new_block)
576	        new_block.parent = container
577	
578	    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
579	        assert block.kind.add_line is not None
580	        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)
581	
582	    def _tip(self) -> Block:
583	        """The deepest open block."""
584	        tip = self.root
585	        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:
586	            tip = child
587	        return tip
588	
589	    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:
590	        child = container.open_last_child()
591	        if child is None:
592	            return
593	        self._close_below(child)
594	        self._finalize(child)
595	
596	    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:
597	        block.is_open = False
598	        if block.kind.finalize is not None:
599	            block.kind.finalize(block)
600	
601	
602	def parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:
603	    """Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters."""
604	    parser = DocumentParser(registry)
605	    for line in lines:
606	        parser.incorporate_line(line)
607	    return parser.finish()

"""Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.

Responsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block
starts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to
`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.

Each block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start
rule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never
names a concrete type.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode
from mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions

TAB_STOP = 4
SPACE_CHARS = " \t"

# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after
# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.
StartRule = Callable[["Cursor", "Block"], "Block | None"]
# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only
# when it returns True.
ContinueRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], bool]
# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.
AddLineRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], None]
# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.
FinalizeRule = Callable[["Block"], None]


def next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:
    """Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop."""
    if char == "\t":
        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP
    return col + 1


def indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:
    """Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`."""
    end = pos
    end_col = col
    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:
        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)
        end += 1
    return end_col - col


class Cursor:
    """A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column."""

    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:
        self.line = line
        self.pos = 0
        self.col = 0

    @property
    def rest(self) -> str:
        """The text from the current position to the end of the line."""
        return self.line[self.pos :]

    @property
    def indent(self) -> int:
        """Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character."""
        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)

    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:
        """Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab."""
        end = self.pos
        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:
            end += 1
        return end

    def is_blank(self) -> bool:
        """True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line."""
        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)

    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column."""
        while self.pos < index:
            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)
            self.pos += 1

    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:
        """Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character."""
        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())

    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:
        """Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.

        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.
        """
        target = self.col + columns
        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:
            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)
            self.pos += 1


class Block:
    """A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close."""

    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:
        self.kind = kind
        self.parent: Block | None = None
        self.children: list[Block] = []
        self.is_open = True
        self.lines: list[str] = []
        self.content = ""
        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.
        self.level = 0
        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.
        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None
        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.
        self.fence: Fence | None = None

    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:
        """The last child if it is still open, otherwise None."""
        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:
            return self.children[-1]
        return None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BlockType:
    """The rules that define one kind of block.

    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such
    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching
    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.
    """

    name: str
    continues: ContinueRule
    is_container: bool = False
    accepts_lines: bool = False
    interruptible: bool = False
    lazy: bool = False
    start: StartRule | None = None
    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None
    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:
            raise ValueError(f"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule")
        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:
            raise ValueError(f"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines")


def _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    return True


def _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    return not cursor.is_blank()


def _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    cursor.advance_nonspace()
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.

    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.
    """
    text = "\n".join(block.lines).strip(" \t")
    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))
    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:
        block.parent.children.remove(block)


def _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:
    """The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to."""
    root = block
    while root.parent is not None:
        root = root.parent
    assert root.references is not None
    return root.references


def _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    return False


THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = "*-_"
THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3


def _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.

    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more
    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= 4:
        return None
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    line = cursor.line
    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:
        return None
    marker = line[start]
    count = 0
    for char in line[start:]:
        if char == marker:
            count += 1
        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:
            return None
    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:
        return None
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)


ATX_MARKER = "#"
ATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6


def _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.

    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the
    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= 4:
        return None
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    end = start
    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:
        end += 1
    level = end - start
    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:
        return None
    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:
        return None
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)
    heading.level = level
    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))
    return heading


def _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:
    """Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.

    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so
    does `foo \\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.
    """
    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)
    if stripped == content:
        return content
    if stripped == "" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:
        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)
    return content


DOCUMENT = BlockType("document", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)
PARAGRAPH = BlockType(
    "paragraph",
    continues=_paragraph_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    interruptible=True,
    lazy=True,
    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,
    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,
)
# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes
# as soon as the next line arrives.
THEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(
    "thematic_break",
    continues=_never_continues,
    start=_thematic_break_start,
)
# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as
# inlines when the document is rendered.
ATX_HEADING = BlockType(
    "atx_heading",
    continues=_never_continues,
    start=_atx_heading_start,
)


CODE_INDENT = 4


def _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.

    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and
    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.
    """
    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:
        return None
    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)


def _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    """A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.

    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.
    """
    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
        return True
    return False


def _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    """Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns."""
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content."""
    lines = list(block.lines)
    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):
        lines.pop()
    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)


# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.
INDENTED_CODE = BlockType(
    "indented_code",
    continues=_indented_code_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    start=_indented_code_start,
    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,
    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,
)


FENCE_CHARS = "`~"
FENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3
BACKTICK = "`"


@dataclass
class Fence:
    """The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.

    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from
    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True
    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing
    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.
    """

    char: str
    length: int
    indent: int
    language: str
    opening: bool = True
    closed: bool = False


def _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:
    """Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`."""
    end = start
    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:
        end += 1
    return end


def _language(info: str) -> str:
    """The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or ""."""
    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()
    return words[0] if words else ""


def _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.

    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.
    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the
    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        return None
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:
        return None
    char = line[start]
    end = _run_end(line, start, char)
    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:
        return None
    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)
    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:
        return None
    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)
    block.fence = fence
    return block


def _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:
    """True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.

    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three
    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        return False
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)
    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)


def _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    """Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.

    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening
    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.
    """
    fence = block.fence
    assert fence is not None
    if fence.closed:
        return False
    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):
        fence.closed = True
        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))
        return True
    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)
    return True


def _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    """Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing."""
    fence = block.fence
    assert fence is not None
    if fence.opening:
        fence.opening = False
        return
    if fence.closed:
        return
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.

    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.
    """
    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in block.lines)


# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's
# container.
FENCED_CODE = BlockType(
    "fenced_code",
    continues=_fenced_code_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    start=_fenced_code_start,
    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,
    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,
)


class BlockRegistry:
    """The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.

    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no
    start rule matches a line of text.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:
        self.root = root
        self.fallback = fallback
        self._names: set[str] = set()
        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []
        self.register(root)
        self.register(fallback)

    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:
        """Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order."""
        if block_type.name in self._names:
            raise ValueError(f"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}")
        self._names.add(block_type.name)
        if block_type.start is not None:
            self._starts.append(block_type)

    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:
        """The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order."""
        return tuple(self._starts)


DEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)


class DocumentParser:
    """Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time."""

    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:
        self.registry = registry
        self.root = Block(registry.root)
        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()

    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:
        """Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text."""
        cursor = Cursor(line)

        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.
        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)
        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None

        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.
        started = False
        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):
            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)
            if new_block is None:
                break
            if not started:
                started = True
                all_closed = True
                self._close_below(container)
            self._attach(new_block, container)
            container = new_block

        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.
        tip = self._tip()
        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:
            self._add_line(tip, cursor)
            return
        self._close_below(container)
        if container.kind.accepts_lines:
            self._add_line(container, cursor)
        elif not cursor.is_blank():
            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)
            self._attach(paragraph, container)
            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)

    def finish(self) -> Block:
        """Close every open block and return the document root."""
        self._close_below(self.root)
        self.root.is_open = False
        return self.root

    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:
        container = self.root
        while True:
            child = container.open_last_child()
            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):
                return container
            container = child

    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
        for block_type in self.registry.starts():
            assert block_type.start is not None
            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)
            if new_block is not None:
                return new_block
        return None

    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:
        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible

    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:
        """Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it."""
        while not container.kind.is_container:
            self._finalize(container)
            assert container.parent is not None
            container = container.parent
        container.children.append(new_block)
        new_block.parent = container

    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
        assert block.kind.add_line is not None
        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)

    def _tip(self) -> Block:
        """The deepest open block."""
        tip = self.root
        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:
            tip = child
        return tip

    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:
        child = container.open_last_child()
        if child is None:
            return
        self._close_below(child)
        self._finalize(child)

    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:
        block.is_open = False
        if block.kind.finalize is not None:
            block.kind.finalize(block)


def parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:
    """Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters."""
    parser = DocumentParser(registry)
    for line in lines:
        parser.incorporate_line(line)
    return parser.finish()

"""Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.

Responsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,
normalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to
`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.
"""

import re
import sys

from mdparser import blocks, inlines, render

REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = "�"
LINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\r\n|\r|\n")


def decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:
    """Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD."""
    return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD."""
    text = text.replace("\x00", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)
    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)


def render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:
    """Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.

    A final line ending terminates the last line rather than starting an empty one, so the one empty
    entry that `split_lines` leaves after it is dropped. Otherwise an unclosed fenced code block would
    gain a blank line.
    """
    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
        lines = lines[:-1]
    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)
    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))


def main() -> int:
    """Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0."""
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    try:
        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))
        html = render_lines(lines)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        html = ""
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode("utf-8"))
    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

exact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.

block tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Block, Fence, parse_lines


def run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        [str(project_root / "commonmark")],
        input=source,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=project_root,
        check=False,
    )


def kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order."""
    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]


def fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[Block]:
    """The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order."""
    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]


def code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order."""
    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]


def fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:
    """The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce."""
    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)
    assert block.fence is not None
    return block.fence

def test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:
    """Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element containing the supplied body."""
    body = "some body text"
    for fence in ("```", "~~~"):
        source = fence + "\n" + body + "\n" + fence + "\n"
        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)
        print(result.stdout)
        assert result.returncode == 0
        assert result.stdout.count("<pre>") == 1
        assert body in result.stdout


def test_fenced_info_string_language_class(project_root: Path) -> None:
    """The first word of the info string becomes the language class."""
    language = "ruby"
    source = "```" + language + " extra words\ncode\n```\n"
    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)
    print(result.stdout)
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert ('class="language-' + language + '"') in result.stdout


def test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:
    """A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not close the block."""
    other = "~~~"
    shorter = "```"
    source = "````\naaa\n" + other + "\n" + shorter + "\n"

## HTML blocks An [HTML block](@) is a group of lines that is treated as raw HTML (and will not be escaped in HTML output). There are seven kinds of [HTML block], which can be defined by their start and end conditions. The block begins with a line that meets a [start condition](@) (after up to three optional spaces of indentation). It ends with the first subsequent line that meets a matching [end condition](@), or the last line of the document, or the last line of the [container block](#container-blocks) containing the current HTML block, if no line is encountered that meets the [end condition]. If the first line meets both the [start condition] and the [end condition], the block will contain just that line. 1. **Start condition:** line begins with the string ``, or the end of the line.\ **End condition:** line contains an end tag ``, ``, ``, or `` (case-insensitive; it need not match the start tag). 2. **Start condition:** line begins with the string ``. 3. **Start condition:** line begins with the string ``. 4. **Start condition:** line begins with the string ``. 5. **Start condition:** line begins with the string ``. 6. **Start condition:** line begins with the string `<` or ``, or the string `/>`.\ **End condition:** line is followed by a [blank line]. 7. **Start condition:** line begins with a complete [open tag] (with any [tag name] other than `pre`, `script`, `style`, or `textarea`) or a complete [closing tag], all on a single line, followed by zero or more spaces and tabs, followed by the end of the line.\ **End condition:** line is followed by a [blank line]. HTML blocks continue until they are closed by their appropriate [end condition], or the last line of the document or other [container block](#container-blocks). This means any HTML **within an HTML block** that might otherwise be recognised as a start condition will be ignored by the parser and passed through as-is, without changing the parser's state. For instance, `
` within an HTML block started by `` will not affect
the parser state; as the HTML block was started in by start condition 6, it
will end at any blank line. This can be surprising:
```````````````````````````````` example



**Hello**,
_world_.




.



**Hello**,

world.




````````````````````````````````
In this case, the HTML block is terminated by the blank line — the `**Hello**`
text remains verbatim — and regular parsing resumes, with a paragraph,
emphasised `world` and inline and block HTML following.
All types of [HTML blocks] except type 7 may interrupt
a paragraph.  Blocks of type 7 cannot interrupt a paragraph.
(This restriction is intended to prevent unwanted interpretation
of long tags inside a wrapped paragraph as starting HTML blocks.)
Some simple examples follow.  Here are some basic HTML blocks
of type 6:
```````````````````````````````` example


  

    
           hi
    
  



okay.
.


  

    
           hi
    
  




okay.

````````````````````````````````

# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,
# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.
AUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r"<([^\x00-\x20\x7f<>]*)>")
# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.
URI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\-]{1,31}:")
# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.
EMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+"
    r"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?"
    r"(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*"
)

# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.
BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r"`+")

# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.
_WS = r"[ \t]*(?:\n[ \t]*)?"
# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.
_WS_REQUIRED = r"(?=[ \t\n])" + _WS
_TAG_NAME = r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\-]*"
_ATTR_NAME = r"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\-]*"
# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.
_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r"[^ \t\n\r\"'=<>`]+"
_ATTR_VALUE = rf"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\")"
_ATTRIBUTE = rf"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?"
# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.
RAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(
    re.compile(pattern)
    for pattern in (
        rf"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>",
        rf"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>",
        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.
        r"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)",
        r"<\?(?s:.*?)\?>",
        r"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>",
        r"<!\[CDATA\[(?s:.*?)\]\]>",
    )
)

"""Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.

Responsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block
starts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to
`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.

Each block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start
rule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never
names a concrete type.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode
from mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions

TAB_STOP = 4
SPACE_CHARS = " \t"

# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after
# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.
StartRule = Callable[["Cursor", "Block"], "Block | None"]
# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only
# when it returns True.
ContinueRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], bool]
# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.
AddLineRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], None]
# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.
FinalizeRule = Callable[["Block"], None]


def next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:
    """Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop."""
    if char == "\t":
        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP
    return col + 1


def indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:
    """Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`."""
    end = pos
    end_col = col
    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:
        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)
        end += 1
    return end_col - col


class Cursor:
    """A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column."""

    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:
        self.line = line
        self.pos = 0
        self.col = 0

    @property
    def rest(self) -> str:
        """The text from the current position to the end of the line."""
        return self.line[self.pos :]

    @property
    def indent(self) -> int:
        """Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character."""
        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)

    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:
        """Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab."""
        end = self.pos
        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:
            end += 1
        return end

    def is_blank(self) -> bool:
        """True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line."""
        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)

    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column."""
        while self.pos < index:
            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)
            self.pos += 1

    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:
        """Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character."""
        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())

    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:
        """Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.

        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.
        """
        target = self.col + columns
        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:
            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)
            self.pos += 1


class Block:
    """A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close."""

    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:
        self.kind = kind
        self.parent: Block | None = None
        self.children: list[Block] = []
        self.is_open = True
        self.lines: list[str] = []
        self.content = ""
        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.
        self.level = 0
        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.
        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None
        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.
        self.fence: Fence | None = None

    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:
        """The last child if it is still open, otherwise None."""
        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:
            return self.children[-1]
        return None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BlockType:
    """The rules that define one kind of block.

    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such
    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching
    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.
    """

    name: str
    continues: ContinueRule
    is_container: bool = False
    accepts_lines: bool = False
    interruptible: bool = False
    lazy: bool = False
    start: StartRule | None = None
    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None
    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:
            raise ValueError(f"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule")
        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:
            raise ValueError(f"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines")


def _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    return True


def _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    return not cursor.is_blank()


def _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    cursor.advance_nonspace()
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.

    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.
    """
    text = "\n".join(block.lines).strip(" \t")
    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))
    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:
        block.parent.children.remove(block)


def _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:
    """The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to."""
    root = block
    while root.parent is not None:
        root = root.parent
    assert root.references is not None
    return root.references


def _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    return False


THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = "*-_"
THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3


def _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.

    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more
    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= 4:
        return None
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    line = cursor.line
    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:
        return None
    marker = line[start]
    count = 0
    for char in line[start:]:
        if char == marker:
            count += 1
        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:
            return None
    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:
        return None
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)


ATX_MARKER = "#"
ATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6


def _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.

    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the
    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= 4:
        return None
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    end = start
    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:
        end += 1
    level = end - start
    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:
        return None
    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:
        return None
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)
    heading.level = level
    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))
    return heading


def _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:
    """Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.

    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so
    does `foo \\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.
    """
    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)
    if stripped == content:
        return content
    if stripped == "" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:
        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)
    return content


DOCUMENT = BlockType("document", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)
PARAGRAPH = BlockType(
    "paragraph",
    continues=_paragraph_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    interruptible=True,
    lazy=True,
    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,
    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,
)
# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes
# as soon as the next line arrives.
THEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(
    "thematic_break",
    continues=_never_continues,
    start=_thematic_break_start,
)
# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as
# inlines when the document is rendered.
ATX_HEADING = BlockType(
    "atx_heading",
    continues=_never_continues,
    start=_atx_heading_start,
)


CODE_INDENT = 4


def _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.

    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and
    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.
    """
    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:
        return None
    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)


def _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    """A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.

    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.
    """
    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
        return True
    return False


def _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    """Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns."""
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content."""
    lines = list(block.lines)
    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):
        lines.pop()
    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)


# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.
INDENTED_CODE = BlockType(
    "indented_code",
    continues=_indented_code_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    start=_indented_code_start,
    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,
    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,
)


FENCE_CHARS = "`~"
FENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3
BACKTICK = "`"


@dataclass
class Fence:
    """The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.

    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from
    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True
    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing
    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.
    """

    char: str
    length: int
    indent: int
    language: str
    opening: bool = True
    closed: bool = False


def _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:
    """Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`."""
    end = start
    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:
        end += 1
    return end


def _language(info: str) -> str:
    """The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or ""."""
    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()
    return words[0] if words else ""


def _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.

    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.
    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the
    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        return None
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:
        return None
    char = line[start]
    end = _run_end(line, start, char)
    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:
        return None
    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)
    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:
        return None
    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)
    block.fence = fence
    return block


def _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:
    """True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.

    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three
    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        return False
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)
    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)


def _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    """Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.

    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening
    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.
    """
    fence = block.fence
    assert fence is not None
    if fence.closed:
        return False
    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):
        fence.closed = True
        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))
        return True
    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)
    return True


def _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    """Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing."""
    fence = block.fence
    assert fence is not None
    if fence.opening:
        fence.opening = False
        return
    if fence.closed:
        return
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.

    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.
    """
    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in block.lines)


# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's
# container.
FENCED_CODE = BlockType(
    "fenced_code",
    continues=_fenced_code_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    start=_fenced_code_start,
    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,
    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,
)


class BlockRegistry:
    """The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.

    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no
    start rule matches a line of text.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:
        self.root = root
        self.fallback = fallback
        self._names: set[str] = set()
        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []
        self.register(root)
        self.register(fallback)

    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:
        """Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order."""
        if block_type.name in self._names:
            raise ValueError(f"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}")
        self._names.add(block_type.name)
        if block_type.start is not None:
            self._starts.append(block_type)

    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:
        """The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order."""
        return tuple(self._starts)


DEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)
DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)


class DocumentParser:
    """Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time."""

    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:
        self.registry = registry
        self.root = Block(registry.root)
        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()

    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:
        """Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text."""
        cursor = Cursor(line)

        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.
        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)
        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None

        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.
        started = False
        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):
            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)
            if new_block is None:
                break
            if not started:
                started = True
                all_closed = True
                self._close_below(container)
            self._attach(new_block, container)
            container = new_block

        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.
        tip = self._tip()
        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:
            self._add_line(tip, cursor)
            return
        self._close_below(container)
        if container.kind.accepts_lines:
            self._add_line(container, cursor)
        elif not cursor.is_blank():
            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)
            self._attach(paragraph, container)
            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)

    def finish(self) -> Block:
        """Close every open block and return the document root."""
        self._close_below(self.root)
        self.root.is_open = False
        return self.root

    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:
        container = self.root
        while True:
            child = container.open_last_child()
            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):
                return container
            container = child

    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
        for block_type in self.registry.starts():
            assert block_type.start is not None
            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)
            if new_block is not None:
                return new_block
        return None

    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:
        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible

    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:
        """Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it."""
        while not container.kind.is_container:
            self._finalize(container)
            assert container.parent is not None
            container = container.parent
        container.children.append(new_block)
        new_block.parent = container

    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
        assert block.kind.add_line is not None
        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)

    def _tip(self) -> Block:
        """The deepest open block."""
        tip = self.root
        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:
            tip = child
        return tip

    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:
        child = container.open_last_child()
        if child is None:
            return
        self._close_below(child)
        self._finalize(child)

    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:
        block.is_open = False
        if block.kind.finalize is not None:
            block.kind.finalize(block)


def parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:
    """Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters."""
    parser = DocumentParser(registry)
    for line in lines:
        parser.incorporate_line(line)
    return parser.finish()

starts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to
`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.

Each block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start
rule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never

# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only
# when it returns True.
ContinueRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], bool]
# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.

def next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:
    """Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop."""
    if char == "\t":
        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP
    return col + 1


def indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:
    """Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`."""
    end = pos
    end_col = col
    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:
        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)
        end += 1
    return end_col - col


class Cursor:
    """A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column."""

    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:
        self.line = line
        self.pos = 0
        self.col = 0

    @property
    def rest(self) -> str:
        """The text from the current position to the end of the line."""
        return self.line[self.pos :]

    @property
    def indent(self) -> int:
        """Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character."""
        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)

    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:
        """Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab."""
        end = self.pos
        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:
            end += 1
        return end

    def is_blank(self) -> bool:
        """True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line."""
        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)

    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column."""
        while self.pos < index:
            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)
            self.pos += 1

    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:
        """Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character."""
        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())

    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:
        """Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.

        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.

        target = self.col + columns
        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:

def _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.

    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more
    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= 4:
        return None
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    line = cursor.line
    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:
        return None
    marker = line[start]
    count = 0
    for char in line[start:]:
        if char == marker:
            count += 1
        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:
            return None
    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:
        return None
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)


ATX_MARKER = "#"
ATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6


def _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.

    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the
    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= 4:
        return None
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    end = start
    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:
        end += 1
    level = end - start
    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:
        return None
    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:
        return None
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)
    heading.level = level
    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))
    return heading


def _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:
    """Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.

    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so
    does `foo \\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.
    """
    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)
    if stripped == content:
        return content
    if stripped == "" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:
        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)
    return content

    continues=_paragraph_continues,

# as soon as the next line arrives.

CODE_INDENT = 4


def _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.

    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and
    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.
    """
    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:
        return None
    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)


def _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    """A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.

    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.
    """
    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)
        return True
    return False


def _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    """Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns."""
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content."""
    lines = list(block.lines)
    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):
        lines.pop()
    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)


# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs
# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.
INDENTED_CODE = BlockType(
    "indented_code",
    continues=_indented_code_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    start=_indented_code_start,
    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,
    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,
)


FENCE_CHARS = "`~"
FENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3
BACKTICK = "`"


@dataclass
class Fence:
    """The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.

    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from
    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True
    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing
    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.
    """

    char: str
    length: int
    indent: int
    language: str
    opening: bool = True
    closed: bool = False


def _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:
    """Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`."""
    end = start
    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:
        end += 1
    return end


def _language(info: str) -> str:
    """The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or ""."""
    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()
    return words[0] if words else ""


def _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:
    """Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.

    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.
    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the
    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        return None
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:
        return None
    char = line[start]
    end = _run_end(line, start, char)
    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:
        return None
    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)
    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:
        return None
    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))
    cursor.advance_to(len(line))
    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)
    block.fence = fence
    return block


def _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:
    """True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.

    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three
    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.
    """
    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:
        return False
    line = cursor.line
    start = cursor.next_nonspace()
    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)
    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)


def _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:
    """Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.

    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening
    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.
    """
    fence = block.fence
    assert fence is not None
    if fence.closed:
        return False
    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):
        fence.closed = True
        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))
        return True
    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)
    return True


def _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:
    """Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing."""
    fence = block.fence
    assert fence is not None
    if fence.opening:
        fence.opening = False
        return
    if fence.closed:
        return
    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)


def _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:
    """Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.

    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.
    """
    block.content = "".join(line + "\n" for line in block.lines)

# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's
# container.
FENCED_CODE = BlockType(
    "fenced_code",
    continues=_fenced_code_continues,
    accepts_lines=True,
    start=_fenced_code_start,

class BlockRegistry:
    """The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.

    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no
    start rule matches a line of text.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:
        self.root = root
        self.fallback = fallback
        self._names: set[str] = set()
        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []
        self.register(root)
        self.register(fallback)

    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:
        """Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order."""
        if block_type.name in self._names:
            raise ValueError(f"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}")
        self._names.add(block_type.name)
        if block_type.start is not None:
            self._starts.append(block_type)

    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:
        """The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order."""
        return tuple(self._starts)
